# Name That LLM — Extra API Passages (new prompts) · v1: Claude models

**Synthetic data.** Every passage in this dataset was generated by a large language model through its official API.

This dataset adds fresh labelled paragraphs for the [Name That LLM](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/name-that-llm) competition. The prompts are **new**, written to resemble the style and domain mix of the competition prompts, they do **not** reuse the competition's training prompts, and they were filtered against its training topics. No competition data (texts, labels or prompts) is included.

v1 covers the **5 Anthropic labels** of the competition, with 1,000 prompts × 5 models (4,998 passages after 2 refusals were dropped). Later versions are planned to add the other providers under the same protocol.

## Files
| File | Rows | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ntl_extra_passages_claude.csv` | 4,998 | One passage per (prompt, model). |
| `prompts.csv` | 1,000 | The prompts: `prompt_id`, `domain`, `task_type`, `topic`, `prompt`. |

### Columns of `ntl_extra_passages_claude.csv`
- `id`: stable 12-character id.
- `prompt_id`: joins to `prompts.csv`. Use it as the **group** in cross-validation, because every prompt has one passage per model.
- `model`: label, using the competition's label names: `claude-fable-5`, `claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`.
- `text`: the passage, a single paragraph.
- `n_words`: number of words in `text`.
- `target_words`: the length requested in the call.
- `domain`, `task_type`, `topic`: copied from the prompt.

## Provenance and collection methodology
- **Source.** Generated by the dataset author through the official Claude API in October 2026. The 5 requested model IDs are the competition's label names, and the model ID returned in every response matched the requested one.
- **Prompts.** The 1,000 English prompts were written for this dataset by an LLM agent workflow, then deduplicated and filtered against the competition's training topics (TF-IDF similarity).
- **Collection.** One generation per (prompt, model) pair: 1,000 × 5 = 5,000 responses. 4,998 were kept; the 2 dropped responses (both `claude-fable-5`) ended with the API stop reason `refusal`. The request format, length sampling and cleanup are listed under *Generation protocol* below.
- **What comes from the competition.** Only the length distribution: each requested length `N` was drawn from the word counts of the competition training passages. No competition texts, labels or prompts, and no scraped or third-party text, are included.

## Generation protocol
- **API.** Official Claude API, October 2026: 4,900 requests through Message Batches and a 100-request pilot (the first 20 prompts) through the standard Messages endpoint, with identical parameters. The model ID returned in every response was checked against the requested one: 0 mismatches.
- **Request.** One user message: `{prompt}` followed by `Write a single paragraph of about N words, with no title or headings.`
  - No system prompt.
  - No temperature or thinking parameters, so each model ran with its API defaults.
  - `max_tokens` 8000.
- **Length.** `N` was drawn per (prompt, model) from the empirical word-count distribution of the competition training passages, so the realised lengths roughly follow the competition's length distribution. Requested lengths run from 36 to 274 words; the passages have a median of 106 words and run from 34 to 297 (98% between 41 and 262).
- **Prompts.** 1,000 prompts across physics, biology, philosophy, mathematics, history, creative prose, computer science, psychology, economics and other fields.
  - Task mix: ~57% explain, ~30% describe/narrate, ~7% argue, ~5% story.
  - Deduplicated and filtered against the competition's training topics.
- **Cleanup.** Light only: whitespace normalisation (a rule to strip a bold wrapper around a whole passage was in place, but no passage needed it). The two responses that ended with stop reason `refusal` were dropped.

## How close is it to the competition data?
A style classifier was trained **only on the competition train set** (character, word, shape and function-word TF-IDF, LinearSVC) and applied to these passages. In the [companion notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/code/seyitkaangunes/does-extra-data-help-ntl-extra-passages) it assigns the correct **provider** to 65% of them and the exact model to 30%. A slightly richer variant (the same TF-IDF views plus typography counts) gives 68% and 31%; on prompt-grouped cross-validation over the competition train set that variant scores about 70% and 38%. This suggests the passages are close to the competition distribution but not identical to it. The host's exact generation settings (system prompt, reasoning settings, length instruction) are unknown.

## Does it help? (quick ablation)
Style-only model (the TF-IDF + LinearSVC above), 5-fold cross-validation **grouped by prompt on the competition train set**. The extra passages are added to every training fold only. They never enter validation, and their prompts are disjoint from the train prompts. Sample weights keep each Claude class's total weight equal to its train weight; `w` is the share of that weight moved to the extra passages. Numbers from the companion notebook:

| w | Balanced accuracy (18-class) | Claude recalls (fable-5 / opus-4-6 / opus-4-8 / opus-5 / sonnet-5) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (train only) | 0.372 | 0.10 / 0.42 / 0.22 / 0.66 / 0.43 |
| 0.25 | 0.380 | 0.17 / 0.55 / 0.29 / 0.72 / 0.53 |
| 0.5 | **0.388** | 0.20 / 0.59 / 0.32 / 0.73 / 0.63 |
| 0.75 | 0.384 | 0.20 / 0.55 / 0.27 / 0.71 / 0.66 |

With the richer variant (plus typography counts) the gain is similar: 0.383 → 0.395 at w = 0.5. The GLM classes, which are stylistically close to Claude, lose some recall when only Claude data is added. Adding the other providers should fix this.

## Companion notebook
[Does extra data help? NTL extra passages](https://www.kaggle.com/code/seyitkaangunes/does-extra-data-help-ntl-extra-passages) uses this dataset on CPU: the fidelity check, the prompt-grouped CV ablation above (the table's numbers), and a submission fitted on the train set plus these passages.

## Updates
v1 (October 2026) covers the 5 Claude labels only. New versions are planned to add the other competition providers under the same protocol. Expected update frequency: monthly while the competition runs (final deadline 2027-01-13); the exact timing is not fixed.

## Limitations
- So far only the 5 Claude labels are covered. If you train on this together with the competition data, use per-class weights so the 18-class balance is not distorted.
- The models ran with their API defaults, which may differ from the host's settings.
- In our tests the gain is clearest for style models. When the style model was blended with strong frozen-LLM features, the blend did not improve in our tests.
- Passages are model outputs and can contain factual errors.
